restrictions: Both colliding messages are exactly 64 bytes: 32 zero bytes followed by a 32-byte little-endian value. They differ in the last 32 bytes.
Full 256-bit digest collision of the three-round target; one compression per message with counter 0, block length 64, flags CHUNK_START|CHUNK_END|ROOT.
Single sequential run with a hard step budget of 2^128.03826 compressions; no restart, no parallelism, no preprocessing, no advice.
Generic birthday-bound search. This entry does not improve the nominal reference blake3-r3-nominal-v2; that identifier is named because the schema requires one.

heuristics.statement: Let A(M, theta, L_max) be the algorithm of Section 3 with fresh-evaluation budget M, distinguished-point density theta and trail cap L_max, run on a function G from n-bit words to n-bit words, and let p_G be its success probability over the uniformly random start words. H1 states: for F : x -> three-round digest of (0^32 || x) at n = 256 with the parameters of Section 3, p_F >= p_rand, where p_rand is the same probability for a uniformly random function. Section 6 computes p_rand >= 0.4047 from two properties of a random function only: among M evaluations at distinct inputs a collision occurs with probability at least 1 - exp(-M (M - 1) / 2^(n+1)), and trail lengths are geometric with parameter theta. H1 says F has at least the first property and the second to within the loss ledger of 6.2. No other heuristic enters the claimed time, memory or success probability; H2 to H4 below concern only how the organizer-executed experiments relate to H1. The time ledger (Section 7) and the memory ledger (Section 4) are hard budgets and do not depend on H1.
heuristics.scope: Used only for the success probability (Section 6: birthday bound 6.1 and loss ledger 6.2) and the table occupancy bound (Section 4). Not used for the time ledger (hard budget) or the memory ledger (fixed allocation). Sensitivity (6.4): the claim survives a collision density down to about 0.953 of random; below that the 0.39 floor is crossed.
heuristics.extrapolation: The organizer-executed experiments are refutation tests, not support. They run the same algorithm with the fresh budget M_w = ceil(sqrt(1.0426 * 2^w)) (M_w^2/2^(w+1) = 0.5317, 0.5237, 0.5217 against 0.5213 at full width) on F restricted to x < 2^w and truncated to its first w bits for w = 12, 16, 18, with theta = 2^-2 and trail cap 64, and compare the host-verified success count out of 256 with the author-measured random-function value q_w (0.3357, 0.3863, 0.3924); fewer than 67, 79, 81 successes respectively refutes H1 at that width. A count at or above the threshold is consistent with H1 at that width and establishes nothing at w = 256, 238 bits beyond the tested widths. The deficits 0.4062 - q_w at small widths come from two loss terms bounded by about 4 M_w / 2^w at the tested theta; theta and the trail count are not scaled across the experiments (H4). Structure giving more collisions than random makes the search faster, not slower; the guarded failure mode is fewer collisions or non-random cycle structure. The step from the tested widths to the claim rests on H2, H3 and H4, declared below.
heuristics.limitations: A width-18 check cannot exclude full-width structure, and three-round BLAKE3 has weak diffusion in its last round. 256 trials have a frequency standard deviation of about 0.03 and cannot resolve a 5 percent density deficit even at the tested width. The author-run reference values q_w and the instance spreads are not organizer-verified. The experiments do not establish p_F >= 0.4047 at any width (they are listed as the refutation tests H1 passed, not as support); no full-width evidence is producible, and this is the obligation every birthday-bound entry on this lane carries.

heuristics.statement: In the organizer-executed experiments, start words derived as the target hash of seed || counter (truncated to w bits) behave, for the success frequency over 256 trials, as independent uniformly random start words, which is what the probability space of proof.md Section 6 assumes.
heuristics.scope: Used only to read the experiment counts as measurements of the Section 3 success probability on F_w. Not used in any claimed number.
heuristics.extrapolation: None. The full-width claim draws its start words uniformly at random (Section 3, step 2); H2 is about the experiments only.
heuristics.limitations: The author's reference values q_w use the same derivation from hashed labels, so a bias in the derivation would be shared by test and reference and not detected. The open run shows the starts reach collisions at the step count predicted for uniform starts, which is weak evidence.

heuristics.statement: F_w, the three-round digest restricted to inputs x < 2^w and truncated to its first w bits, is a representative stand-in for F at n = 256 for the purpose of refuting H1: a collision-density deficit at full width would show as a deficit at the tested widths.
heuristics.scope: Used only to relate the experiments to H1. Not used in any claimed number.
heuristics.extrapolation: From widths 12, 16, 18 to width 256, 238 bits beyond the largest tested width; from a message family in which only word 8 and the low bits of word 9 vary to the full 256-bit family; from the first digest word to the full digest.
heuristics.limitations: No evidence beyond the three widths. Three-round BLAKE3 has weak diffusion in its last round, so a prefix of the digest may be less or more random-like than the full digest. This is the gap every reduced-width test on this lane carries.

heuristics.statement: Running the Section 3 algorithm with theta = 2^-2 and 16 to 130 trails per run tests the same collision-density property that H1 guards at theta = 2^-115 and 8364 trails; the trail-structure part of H1 is tested only at theta = 2^-2.
heuristics.scope: Used only to relate the experiments to H1. Not used in any claimed number.
heuristics.extrapolation: From theta = 2^-2 to theta = 2^-115 and from trails of mean length 4 to trails of mean length 2^115. The loss terms of Section 6.2 that depend on theta are bounded at full width by the geometric trail-length model, not by the experiments.
heuristics.limitations: The experiments say nothing about the cycle structure of F on trails of length 2^115. The deficits 0.4062 - q_w following the theta-dependent loss bounds at the tested widths is consistency, not evidence about full-width trail structure.
